audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers hand Ambessa levels 4-5 (side "Skill") while their own prose calls that window her weakest and Poppy's strongest, and both give Poppy the first-item stage while whys[5] concludes it is "even at best". phases[3].why is generic filler ("bank small leads") that says nothing about this lane.
audit.why: At 45.6% over 193 games Ambessa is behind, but the shape matters more than the sign: Steadfast Presence is 20s at rank 1 and drops to 12s at rank 5, so Poppy's dash-denial gets strictly more frequent exactly through levels 4-5 while Ambessa's Lacerate (13/12/11/10/9) and Repudiation (18/17/16/15/14) are still near their longest. That is why 4-5 is Poppy's, not shared.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 flipped to Poppy in both layers, first item flipped to Skill, and phases[3].why rewritten to name the real reason. Level 6 should also read Ambessa in both layers — both narratives already say so — but "Skill"->"Ambessa" is outside the length band, so it is left for the user.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike list never gives a single cooldown number, so "bait her W then commit" has no clock attached to it. spikes[0] says W "comes online" without saying how long the window between casts is.
audit.why: Steadfast Presence is 20/18/16/14/12s. At level 2 that is a twenty-second gap — enormous, and the whole reason the early weave is still playable if you spend a throwaway cast to draw it. By rank 5 it is twelve seconds and the window effectively closes. Heroic Charge is 14/13/12/11/10 and Keeper's Verdict 140/120/100.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into spikes[0], wants.you[2], breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (a) phases[1].why says "Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade" — Drakehound's Step grants no shield. (b) The consequence of a stopped dash is never stated anywhere: Steadfast Presence does not merely cancel it, it slows and grounds you afterwards. (c) Keeper's Verdict is a channel and Public Execution suppresses, but nothing in the entry connects the two; dontsFull[2] is titled "Get R-knocked mid-combo" and then describes dumping dashes instead. dosFull[2] and dontsFull[1] have the same title/description mismatch.
audit.why: Riot's Drakehound's Step text grants bonus range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund — the shield in Ambessa's kit is Repudiation (W). Riot's Steadfast Presence text: "stop enemy dashes around her. If a dash is stopped, the enemy is slowed and grounded" — so a failed weave costs you the follow-up too, which is the actual reason the ability is matchup-defining. Keeper's Verdict is a channelled hammer strike and suppression is hard CC, so Public Execution takes her out of the wind-up.
audit.corrected: Passive shield claim removed; the slow-and-ground consequence written into spikes[0], whys[1], wants.foe[0] and report[5]; the Keeper's Verdict channel/suppress interaction added to spikes[3] and dontsFull[2]; the three mismatched do/don't descriptions repaired to match their titles.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json (P: bonus range, damage, attack speed, energy refund; W is the shield)
champ-data/_kits/poppy.json (W stopped-dash slow+ground; R channel, cd 140/120/100)

audit.whatIsWrong: Iron Ambassador is never mentioned. The entry lists Plated Steelcaps and Heart of Steel as the reason your burst falls off but omits the free shield she re-arms every time she walks over the bounced buckler.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: "Poppy throws her buckler that bounces off the target. Poppy can pick it up to gain a temporary shield." Against a burst pattern that has to land inside one empowered-auto window, a shield she can deny you by walking three hundred units is worth naming. _missing-interactions.json flags it under shield-absorbs-burst and it is a true positive.
audit.corrected: Added to spikes[2] alongside the armour items.

audit.why: _missing-interactions.json also flags "Poppy can go untargetable through your commit (Keeper's Verdict (R))". That is a FALSE POSITIVE — Riot's text for Keeper's Verdict is "channels a hammer strike that knocks enemies very far away" with no untargetability, and the kit file's "untargetable" flag is a bad derivation. I wrote no wait-it-out advice on that basis.

notes:
KIT-FILE DATA WARNING that affects every Ambessa matchup, not just this one: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json carries a spurious "heal" flag and a spurious "grounding" flag on Public Execution, and a spurious "grounding" flag on Repudiation. Riot's own text for both abilities contains no healing and no grounding — the parser appears to have fired on the words "slams the ground". I wrote no anti-heal or grounding advice for Ambessa anywhere. _missing-interactions.json propagates the heal error into other matchups.

Second kit-file misfire, this one on Poppy: "grounding" is flagged on Hammer Shock (Q) and "untargetable" on Keeper's Verdict (R). Neither appears in Riot's description of those abilities. Q slows, R knocks back.

FALSE POSITIVE in the packet: suspectNames flags "With Steadfast Presence" in spikes[3] at distance 5. The ability name written there is correct; the distance comes from the leading word "With".

COULD NOT FIT IN THE BAND, for the user to apply by hand: Level 6 should read "Ambessa" in content win[4] and full phases[4].side. Both layers' prose already says level 6 is Ambessa's one clean window, and the packet levelChart agrees, but "Skill" (5 chars) to "Ambessa" (7) is outside +/-10% so the applier would reject it.

UNVERIFIED, deliberately left alone: spikes[1], wants.you[1] and whys[4] all assert that Public Execution lands "regardless of W" / "through W". Riot calls the R a blink, and Steadfast Presence stops dashes — but whether Ambessa's R is classified as a dash for that check is not answerable from the kit files, so I did not touch those three strings.
